styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Elbphilharmonie, Speicherstadt and the big museums.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Harbour history, St. Pauli and the war years.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Fish sandwiches, Franzbrötchen and harbour-side dinners.

stays.why: Central for the Rathaus, Kunsthalle and the lake. Walk to the main station and U/S-Bahn.
Next to the Elbphilharmonie and Speicherstadt. New hotels, quiet nights, short walk to the water.
Nightlife, the Reeperbahn and the harbour edge. Lively and loud on weekends.
Local feel, good food, river views from the Elbe beach. Quick S-Bahn ride to the centre.

food: Try a Fischbrötchen (fish sandwich) at the Landungsbrücken or the fish market; prices are roughly €4–8.
Franzbrötchen is the local cinnamon pastry. Buy one warm from a bakery for about €2–3.
Labskaus and Grünkohl are classic Hamburg dishes; look for them on traditional restaurant menus.
The Sunday fish market in Altona (early morning) is a Hamburg ritual; check opening hours on the day.
Book ahead for dinner on the Reeperbahn or in HafenCity on weekends; walk-ins get harder after 19:00.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a harbour ferry ride on the Elbe; regular ferries run and are cheap with a transit ticket.
Add a day trip to the Speicherstadt museums or the International Maritime Museum if you like ships.
Planten un Blomen park and the Wallanlagen are free and good for a slow half-day in dry weather.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Elbphilharmonie, Speicherstadt, the harbour and a good food evening; add a third for museums and a ferry.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 5°C, lows around 0°C. Pack a warm coat and waterproof shoes.
February: still cold, highs near 7°C. Short days; plan indoor sights.
March: cool at 9°C highs, about 11 rain days. Layers help.
April: milder, highs near 13°C. Good for walking the harbour.
May: pleasant, highs near 18°C. Busy weekends; book hotels early.
June: warm, highs near 22°C, about 11 rain days. Long evenings.
July: warmest month, highs near 23°C, but about 14 rain days. Keep a rain jacket handy.
August: warm at 23°C highs, about 13 rain days. Peak season for the harbour.
September: still mild, highs near 20°C. Fewer rain days; a good shoulder month.
October: cooler, highs near 14°C, about 14 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
November: cold and wet, highs near 9°C. Dark early; plan indoor time.
December: cold, highs near 6°C, about 14 rain days. Christmas markets are the draw; dress warm.

climate_guide.summary: Cool and changeable: mild summers, cold winters, and rain in every month. Pack layers and rain gear year-round.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect 10–14 rain days every month. A light waterproof jacket beats an umbrella in wind.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Highs around 20–23°C and long days. The busiest and most comfortable season.

items.title: Winter is cold, not extreme
items.text: January highs near 5°C and lows around 0°C. A warm coat, hat and gloves are enough.

items.title: Wind off the Elbe
items.text: Harbour and waterfront areas feel colder and windier than the city centre. Layer up.

items.title: Shoulder months are mild but wet
items.text: April, May, September and October are pleasant for walking, with frequent showers.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket, comfortable walking shoes and a warm hat for winter.

transit.best: S-Bahn and U-Bahn for most trips; walk or cycle in the flat centre.

modes.text: S-Bahn and U-Bahn cover the city. Buy a ticket before boarding; day tickets start around €8.20.
Buses fill the gaps. Buy your ticket before boarding; no ticket sales on board.
Metered taxis are plentiful. Uber and Bolt work too.
Driving is slow with roadworks and costly parking. Use park-and-ride if you must drive.
The city is flat and good for walking and cycling. Ferries cross the Elbe.
Ferries cross the Elbe and are a cheap way to see the harbour.
